# Contributing to Secuura

Thank you for your interest in contributing to Secuura. This document outlines the process and standards for contributing to the project.

---

## Development Setup

### Prerequisites

- **Docker Desktop** v24+ with Docker Compose v2
- **Node.js** v18+ and npm v9+
- **Git**

### Getting Started

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone <repo-url>
cd Dev

# Install dependencies
npm ci

# Copy environment files
cp env.example .env
cp .env.local.example .env.local

# Start infrastructure and all services
docker compose up -d
```

The platform is accessible at `http://localhost:6882` once all services are healthy.

---

## Branching Model — Git Flow

> **Work is organised by stream.** Every ticket belongs to exactly one Linear project, and Peter is handed
> a **stream** to test rather than a ticket at a time (Kam, 2026-09-02). Branch and PR granularity are
> unchanged by that — what changes is that a stream's evidence lives in one place and is tested once. The
> rule, the three dispositions and the archive-never-close policy are stated once, in
> [`docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` § Work is organised by stream](./docs/DEV-PROCESS.md#work-is-organised-by-stream-not-by-ticket-kam-2026-09-02) —
> deliberately cited rather than repeated here, so there is one copy to keep true.

Adopted 2026-05-25 (Linear KS-137). `main` is the **stability / production** branch and is always
releasable — **feature work never branches from, or merges directly into, `main`.**

### Long-lived branches

| Branch | Role |
|--------|------|
| `main` | Stability / production. Only `release/*` and `hotfix/*` merge here. Always releasable; tagged at each version. |
| `develop` | Integration line. All feature work branches from, and merges back into, `develop`. |

### Supporting branches

| Branch | Cut from | Merges into | Purpose |
|--------|----------|-------------|---------|
| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` | New features, fixes, chores during normal development. |
| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` | Stabilise a version; tag on `main`, then back-merge into `develop`. |
| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` | Urgent production fix. Folds back into both so the fix can't be lost (no crossover). |

```
   feature/* ──► develop ──► release/* ──► main ──(tag vX.Y)
                   ▲                         │
                   └──────── back-merge ─────┤
                                             │
                 hotfix/* ◄── main ──────────┘
                   └──► main + develop  (fold-back)
```

**Why:** in-progress work (e.g. a v2.0 line on `develop`) stays off the released branch, so a `vX`
hotfix ships from a branch off `main` without exposing unreleased work — and the fold-back keeps
`main` and `develop` from diverging.

### Branch naming

- **Ticketed work (default):** use the **Linear-suggested `gitBranchName` verbatim** so ticket ↔ branch
  matches — e.g. `kamilkreiser/ks-137-adopt-document-git-flow-...` (Linear issue → "Copy git branch name").
- **Untracked work only:** fall back to a typed prefix — `feature/`, `fix/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`,
  `test/`, `chore/` (e.g. `fix/auth-session-expiry`).
- Keep branches short-lived; delete after merge.

### Gate

Nothing reaches `main` or a `release/*` branch without the **pre-merge gate green on the exact merge
commit** (Linear KS-105). That is what keeps `main` releasable by construction — the branching model
and the CI gate stack; neither replaces the other.

### How the required checks behave on `hotfix/*` → `main` (KS-383)

`main` doesn't carry the real `pr-*` suites (they live on the integration line and arrive with each
release). The KS-380 required checks report on main-base PRs like this:

- **Config/docs-only hotfix** (workflows, dependabot, `*.md`, …): the no-op twins report the four
  path-gated checks, and `pr-security-gates-main-bootstrap.yml` reports Code Security Gates by running
  the gate scripts that exist at main-age. Green → mergeable.
- **Platform-touching hotfix** (`services/`, `frontend/`, `packages/`, …): the real suites don't exist
  on main's merge ref, so those checks never report and the PR stays BLOCKED. **This is deliberate** —
  platform fixes go out through a `release/*` (which carries the full suites), or the hotfix must
  cherry-pick the real workflow files onto its branch so the suites actually run on the merge ref.
- **Known residual:** a *mixed* hotfix (platform code + a path the twins match, e.g. a `.md` or
  `.github/**` file) gets twin-green without the real suite — same-name/latest-report semantics only
  self-correct where the real workflow exists. Hotfix review must eyeball the diff for this shape.
- **Merge method:** `hotfix/*` and `release/*` PRs use **merge commits** (not squash) — the
  fold-back/tombstone mechanics below depend on shared history. Feature PRs into `develop` stay squash.
- **No force push (KS-1037):** `.githooks/pre-push` REFUSES any non-fast-forward push to a branch that
  already exists at origin — a rebase becomes a NEW branch. Why: a force push rewrites history another
  process may depend on — an open PR's head, or a gate running against the SHA being replaced.
  - `ALLOW_FORCE=1 git push …` is the escape, for the deliberate case only, stated explicitly.
  - Scope (Kam's standing ruling, 2026-09-07, narrow-allow): permitted on your OWN unshared branch with no PR
    and no live gate; anything shared — `develop`, `main`, a branch with an open PR — stays as it is.
  - Behind or `dirty`? Merge `develop` INTO the branch, do not rebase: it is a fast-forward, keeps the PR and
    its review thread, and the merge commit collapses at squash time. One cost: any new commit makes an existing approval stale.
- The bootstrap workflow lives **only on the main line**; the KS-383 fold-back removed it from
  `develop`, so the first `release/*` merge into `main` deletes it and installs the real
  `pr-security-gates.yml`. Don't re-add it to `develop`.

> **Rollout (KS-137):** `develop` is being cut as part of adoption. Until it exists, branch from `main`
> and note the bootstrap on the ticket. Once `develop` is the default base, set it as the GitHub default
> branch for new PRs and point branch protection at both `main` and `develop`. The mapping of
> `main` / `develop` (and the existing `demo` branch) to the Azure dev/demo deploys is a separate
> team decision — track it alongside the deploy workflow, don't assume it here.

---

## Shared-stack safety (KS-666)

The VM hosts **one** platform stack, and before KS-666 the routine recovery path
— `docker compose down -v` followed by `git checkout develop` — checked nothing.
It did not ask whether the stack was occupied, who owned it, which branch it was
on, or whether the tree held uncommitted work. On 2026-08-19 a planned rebuild
was one command away from destroying another developer's 35-container stack,
their seeded volumes, and an uncommitted file that no git operation could have
recovered. Nothing would have errored; the rebuild would have reported success.

### Use the named destructive paths, not raw compose

| Intent | Command |
| -- | -- |
| Stop the stack, keep data | `./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --stop` |
| Stop and **destroy volumes** | `./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --fresh-db` |
| Rebuild images and restart | `./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` |

All three run `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_guard.sh` first. `docker compose
down -v` typed by hand runs nothing and is exactly the reflex this replaced.

### What the guard checks

It reads the ownership labels — carried by **every** service, plus a dedicated
`stack-marker` container that keeps them readable while the rest of the stack is
down — and refuses when either is true:

* the stack belongs to **someone else** — it prints their name, branch, commit,
  start time (ISO 8601 UTC) and the container count;
* your working tree has **uncommitted tracked changes** — it lists them.

Labels are read from the live container rather than a lease file on purpose: a
label dies with the stack, so it cannot survive a crash and go stale. A stale
lease is worse than none, because people learn to ignore it.

A stack started by a bare `docker compose up` records `owner=unknown`. That is
treated as *unowned*, not as a foreign owner — blocking on it would fire on
every hand-started stack, and a guard that always fires gets trained out.

### Overriding

```bash
./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --fresh-db --i-have-confirmed-with-the-owner
```

The flag is deliberately long, and every use is written to syslog with your
username and the previous owner and branch.

**An override is legitimate when** you have actually spoken to the person named
in the refusal and they have confirmed they are finished; or the refusal names a
stack you know to be abandoned (the owner has gone home, the branch is merged)
and you have said so in the team channel.

**It is not legitimate** because the guard is inconvenient, because you assume
nobody else is working, or because the dirty file "looks generated". If the tree
is dirty and the changes are not yours, they belong to someone — commit them to
a scratch branch or stash them before you override, because after the override
they are unrecoverable.

### Why the tree must stay clean

The uncommitted-changes check is only worth having if a clean tree is the normal
state. Akto's `scripts/start.sh` used to regenerate
`systemTest/akto/src/core/aktoUpgradeTestIdCatalog.generated.ts` into the working tree on
every bootstrap, so the tree was dirty as a matter of course and the check would
have been permanently true. That step is now read-only (`npm run check-test-ids`,
which renders and compares outside the repo), regeneration is an explicit
`npm run generate-test-ids`, and CI fails when the committed catalog is stale.

**Rule: stack start-up must never write into the working tree.** If you add a
bootstrap step that generates a tracked file, it belongs behind an explicit
command with a CI staleness gate, not in the start path.

### Running more than one stack — stack slots

`SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` selects an isolated stack:

```bash
SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=2 ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh
```

* **Four slots, and the numbering is shared with platform-s** (PS-622). Every
  published port is the historic one plus `100 * (N - 1)`, so **platform-s slot N
  and platform-k slot N pair up with no extra configuration** — the gateway lands
  on 6882 · 6982 · 7082 · 7182. platform-s exports `STACK_SLOT`, which this
  honours, so a single export in a worktree drives both platforms.
* **Slot 1 is the default and is unchanged** — same ports (6882 / 6432 / 6379),
  same compose project, same volumes, same artifact paths. Nothing that hardcodes
  those breaks.
* **Slot N > 1** offsets every published port by `100 * (N - 1)` and uses its own
  compose project name, container prefix, network and volumes. A `--fresh-db` of
  one slot therefore cannot reach another slot's data.
* **A requested slot retargets a LOCAL harness URL, even one already configured.**
  `systemTest/akto/.env.example` ships `SECUURA_API_URL=http://localhost:6882`, so
  a configured value is usually present; if it always won, asking for slot 2 would
  leave the harness on slot 1 and the report would describe the wrong stack. A
  *remote* URL (demo, staging, a tunnel) is a deliberate choice about a different
  environment and is never overridden.

Pair a slot with its own git worktree so a checkout can never move beneath a
running stack:

```bash
git worktree add ~/dev/wt/ks-123 -b feature/ks-123-... origin/develop
cd ~/dev/wt/ks-123
SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=2 ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh
```

This is what makes concurrent work on platform-k possible at all: one clone,
one tree and one port set is a hard ceiling of one session, regardless of spare
VM capacity.

**Capacity is a separate question from isolation.** Slots give you namespacing
and safety immediately; whether the VM sustains two full stacks (35+ containers
each) is unmeasured. Measure before assuming, and expect to need a reduced
service subset for the second slot.

### How this is kept from being reverted

Nearly all of the above is shell scripts and compose YAML, where an edit can undo
the protection without breaking anything visible — the stack still starts, the
tests still pass, and the guard is simply gone until the next collision. Three
gates run on every PR (`pr-security-gates.yml`, mirrored in `security-scan.yml`):

| Gate | What it proves |
| -- | -- |
| `scripts/check-stack-safety.sh` | the protection is still **wired in** — marker + labels, guard invoked on every destructive path, both scripts sourcing `stack_env.sh`, teardown defaults, ports parameterised, and (KS-1096) `start-secuura.sh`'s health wait / `--status` / DB+Redis probes / port pre-flight derived from `STACK_PREFIX` and the per-slot ports rather than slot 1's bare names and 6432/6379 |
| `scripts/__tests__/stack_guard.test.sh` | what the guard **does** — 17 cases over a stubbed docker and temp repos |
| `scripts/__tests__/stack_env.test.sh` | the slot → ports/project **mapping** — 20 cases, including that slot 1 never moves |
| `scripts/check-akto-container-names.sh` (called by `check-stack-safety.sh` as 6f2) | no Akto harness file names a slot-1 container — literally **or as a defaulted variable** (`${VAR:-akto-mongo}`, `?? 'akto-testing'`) — across `src/` + `bin/` + `scripts/`, `*.ts`/`*.sh`/`*.mjs`. Its non-vacuity assert names the directories and extensions the corpus **must** contribute and fails when one is absent — coverage, not a file count, because a count passed over the directory KS-687 F1 lived in. Pinned red-first by `scripts/__tests__/check_akto_container_names.test.sh` (17 cases; F1's original line is the first) |

All four are pure shell against stubs: no Docker daemon, no stack boot. If you
change stack orchestration and one fails, it is telling you a safety property was
dropped — fix the property, not the test. If you genuinely intend to change a
property, change the assertion in the same commit and say why.

### What is still not protected

The guard is **advisory**. `docker compose down -v` typed directly bypasses it,
and daemon-wide operations are globally destructive across every slot. In
particular:

> **Never run `docker system prune -a --volumes` on a shared host.** It ignores
> project namespacing and destroys every stack on the machine.

`STACK_OWNER` is self-reported: without per-user accounts on the VM it is
whatever account the operator used, which caps how far the ownership half of the
guard can be trusted. That is an organisational fix, not a technical one.

---

## Commit Style

This project follows **Conventional Commits** (https://www.conventionalcommits.org):

```
<type>(<scope>): <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]
```

### Types

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `feat` | A new feature |
| `fix` | A bug fix |
| `docs` | Documentation only |
| `style` | Formatting, no code change |
| `refactor` | Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature |
| `test` | Adding or correcting tests |
| `chore` | Build process, CI, dependencies |
| `perf` | Performance improvement |

### Scopes

Use the service or module name: `auth`, `originate`, `api-gateway`, `admin`, `issuer`, `shared`, `docker`, `ci`, etc.

### Examples

```
feat(auth): add MFA backup codes support
fix(anchoring): handle Blockfrost 429 rate-limit response
docs(api): update OpenAPI spec for billing endpoints
test(transfer): add delegation service unit tests
chore(docker): pin Redis image to 7.2-alpine
```

---

## Test Requirements

**All tests must pass before a pull request can be merged.**

```bash
# Run all unit tests
npm test

# Run service-specific tests
npm test -w services/originate

# Run E2E tests (requires services running)
npx playwright test

# Run smoke tests
./scripts/smoke-test.sh

# Run ONE test file (fastest loop while writing a regression test)
cd services/originate && npx jest src/__tests__/ks694-nodeenv-role-gate-bypass.test.ts
```

### Test expectations

- New features must include unit tests
- Bug fixes must include a regression test
- Never skip tests -- treat skips as failures and fix them
- Aim for meaningful coverage of business logic, not arbitrary percentage targets

**A regression test must be red on the broken code and green after the fix, and the PR records
both numbers.** Run the new test against the pre-fix behaviour (restore the old line, then re-run
the same file), quote the split, then run it again with the fix. A test that was never seen to fail
proves nothing about the fix. Worked example, incl. how to reproduce the red half: the header
comment of `services/originate/src/__tests__/ks694-nodeenv-role-gate-bypass.test.ts`.

**Some service suites carry failures that are not yours.** Before attributing a red to your branch,
check `BACKLOG.md` (the "pre-existing failures" entries), then confirm by stashing your branch and
re-running the same file on the clean tree. Record the outcome honestly in the PR's Test Evidence
block — "374 passed, 2 failed, both pre-existing on `develop` (verified by stashing)" is a complete
line; "tests pass" is not.

**The four platform suites are a separate, later gate** — see [Adopted merge flow](#adopted-merge-flow-kam-2026-08-25--the-standing-flow)
below, and the runbook (commands, preconditions, and the four ways those results mislead) in
[`systemTest/CLAUDE.md` → The four-suite final check before review](../../systemTest/CLAUDE.md#the-four-suite-final-check-before-review-ks-685).

---

## Pull Request Process

### Pre-push preflight (KS-380) — run before every push

`bash scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` (from `Blockchain/Dev`) runs the fast,
cross-cutting checks that the per-package test suites don't — the exact class
of mistake recent builds leaked to reviewers:

| Check | Catches | Slip it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAPI spec drift (`check:openapi`) | generated spec out of sync with the Zod source | stale-spec-makes-checks-lie |
| Lockfile clean-room (`lockfile-cleanroom.sh`) | standalone locks that only install under workspace hoisting | KS-374 / KS-376 / #399 |
| Spec-auth conformance (`spec-auth-conformance.mjs`) | a bearer-authed operation answering unauthenticated | **KS-375** |

Run it before pushing a feature branch; the auth leg needs the local stack up
on `:6882` (it skips cleanly otherwise). It does **not** replace `npm test` or
the systemTest gates — it's the structural sweep on top of them.

**Auto-run it on push (recommended).** A `pre-push` hook runs the preflight for
any push that touches `Blockchain/Dev`, and no-ops otherwise. Enable once per
clone (from the repo root):

```sh
git config core.hooksPath .githooks && chmod +x .githooks/pre-push
```

The hook degrades gracefully — a leg whose dependency is down (Docker off →
lockfile leg advisory; stack off → auth leg skipped) never blocks a push; CI is
the hard gate. Bypass a single push with `git push --no-verify`.

**Working from a `git worktree`? Run `npm ci` in it once (KS-691).** `node_modules`
is gitignored and the root `package-lock.json` places ~218 dependencies in *nested*
trees — `packages/shared` carries its own `@types/node ^20` because the root hoists
26. A fresh worktree has none of them, and the two failure modes are different:

- **Nothing installed** — `tsc` isn't on `PATH`, and the drift leg reports
  `STALE — … this is an install problem, NOT spec drift` with the fix. Correct
  since KS-469; measured again in a pristine worktree on 2026-08-31.
- **Partially installed** — root tree present, nested absent, which is what an
  interrupted `npm ci` or a hand-symlinked `node_modules` leaves. `tsc` then
  resolves the hoisted `@types/node 26`, which dropped `crypto.JsonWebKey`, and
  fails in `packages/shared/src/crypto/jwks.ts`. Because that is a *successful
  compile producing a type error*, it matched none of the install-failure
  signatures and was announced as `FAIL — spec drifted` on a spec that had not
  drifted. `scripts/preflight/deps-present.sh` now catches it first.

One `npm ci` from `Blockchain/Dev` covers both — run it **there**, never from
inside `packages/shared` (npm resolves the workspace root and installs only that
member's closure, pruning `tsx` — KS-469). The standalone `scripts/preflight` and
`scripts/audit` members install themselves on first run.

1. Target the correct base — `develop` for `feature/*`, `main` for `release/*` and `hotfix/*` — and ensure your branch is up to date with it (see Branching Model above)
2. Run `bash scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` and clear anything it flags
3. Run `npm test` and confirm all tests pass
4. Run `npm run lint` (if configured) and fix any issues
5. Verify your changes work with `docker compose up -d`

### Adopted merge flow (Kam, 2026-08-25) — the standing flow

**Adopted by Kam on 2026-08-25**: *"Happy with that   Work this into our current
flow and follow it going forward."* It is Stuart's proposal with Peter's
amendments, and it is the standing flow — permanently, now that GitHub Actions is
retired (Kam, 2026-08-27).

**Team-facing version.** The same flow written up for the team — five stages,
two roles, plus the CI-outage gate, the review-capacity constraint and the rule
for agent-authored PRs — is at [`docs/DEV-PROCESS.md`](docs/DEV-PROCESS.md)
(v4 · 11 September 2026 — Kam ruled that we approve our own work (16:56)). This section stays the contributor-facing copy,
and the two agree on the adopted flow. **One item in that document differs and is
flagged there as a proposal, not yet team-agreed** — *approval may come from any
of the three who is not the author*.

1. Develop on a branch.
2. **Test your own work before the PR goes up**, and put the results in the PR
   description — see the **Test Evidence** block in the template below.
3. Commit → push → open the PR.
4. Peter runs periodic formal test passes; demo (UAT) is updated after his nod.
5. Findings from the QA gate are discussed with the PR issuer.
6. **The author merges once the PR is TESTED — not the reviewer.** TESTED = a QA
   gate verdict (GO or GO WITH FINDINGS) at the PR's current head + a Test Evidence
   block + our own suites, and **Wednesday's GO, naming the head SHA, is the approval** (Kam, 2026-09-11):
   16:56:00 *"For the time being, I / you will approve our own elements"* ·
   16:56:44 *"based on this.  FIx and merge all tickets after they are tested"* ·
   16:58:04 *"yes, still run all our own tests to make sure we only commit things that are working and tested."*
   This keeps `develop` moving when anyone is away, and puts the person best
   placed to fix a post-merge break in control of when it happens.
7. Pull `develop`, then **manual deploy by the PR issuer** where one applies — demo (UAT) only after Peter's nod.

**The ticket and the review must not sit with the same person.** An authoring seat cannot
sign off its own work: the sign-off is the QA gate verdict at head plus Wednesday's GO
(Kam, 2026-09-11).

**Untested, or no GO → no merge.** Never push straight to `develop`.

#### ⚠ `mergeable_state: clean` is NOT evidence that anything was tested

GitHub reporting a PR as **clean** means only that no required check is currently
failing or pending. **It does not mean a check ran.** With Actions retired no
check runs at all, so every PR reads `clean` or `unstable` for reasons that have
nothing to do with whether the code works.

Under this flow the **Test Evidence block is what carries the testing claim** —
`mergeable_state` carries none of it. Treating "clean" as green certifies
untested code and reports it as verified. (KS-660 exists precisely to bannerise
this.)

### PR Description Template

```markdown
## Summary

Brief description of what changed and why.

## Changes

- Bullet list of specific changes

## Test Evidence

Required on every PR (Kam-adopted 2026-08-25). It does not need to be an essay —
it needs to be honest.

- **Touched:** which services / packages / files
- **Ran:** which suites actually executed, and their results
- **NOT run:** what you did not get to, and why
- **Migrations / config:** any schema change, env var, or config this needs

### Platform suites — final check (Kam's rule 2026-08-27)

- **Schemathesis:** run/result | not run + why
- **Akto:** run/result | not run + why
- **Playwright:** run/result | not run + why
- **Performance / k6:** run/result | not run + why
- **Unit suites (touched services):** run/result | not run + why

A "NOT run" line is the point of this block, not an embarrassment in it —
because the QA gate reads it and needs to know where to look.
- **Preflight (the pre-push hook, .githooks/pre-push):** N/13 legs ran | NOT RUN + why — the hook skips vault-only,
  docs-only and systemTest-only pushes SILENTLY (KS-1049), so a pushed PR is not evidence the gate ran

## Test Plan

- [ ] Unit tests pass
- [ ] E2E tests pass (if applicable)
- [ ] Manual testing completed
- [ ] No skipped tests introduced

## Related Issues

Closes #<issue-number>
```

## Code Style

### TypeScript

- **Strict mode** enabled (`"strict": true` in all `tsconfig.json` files)
- The following incremental strict flags are explicitly set across all services, packages, and apps:
  - `"noImplicitAny": true` -- catches implicit `any` types (included in `strict`)
  - `"strictNullChecks": true` -- catches null/undefined errors (included in `strict`)
  - `"noUnusedLocals": true` -- flags unused local variables as errors
  - `"noUnusedParameters": true` -- flags unused function parameters as errors
- Do not weaken these settings (e.g., setting `noUnusedLocals: false`) without team discussion
- Use `interface` for object shapes, `type` for unions and intersections
- Prefer `const` over `let`; avoid `var`
- Use async/await over raw Promises
- All public functions should have JSDoc comments

### ESLint

Follow the project ESLint configuration. Fix all linting errors before submitting.

```bash
npm run lint        # Check for issues
npm run lint:fix    # Auto-fix where possible
```

### Naming Conventions

| Item | Convention | Example |
|------|-----------|---------|
| Files | kebab-case | `document-repo.ts` |
| Classes | PascalCase | `DocumentRepository` |
| Functions | camelCase | `getDocumentById` |
| Constants | UPPER_SNAKE_CASE | `MAX_RETRY_COUNT` |
| Database tables | snake_case | `blockchain_anchors` |
| Environment variables | UPPER_SNAKE_CASE | `DATABASE_URL` |

### Project Structure

- Backend services live in `services/<name>/`
- Frontend apps live in `frontend/<name>/`
- Shared packages live in `packages/shared/`
- Database schemas live in `docker/init/`

---

## Docker Guidelines

- All services must include a health check
- Use multi-stage builds to minimize image size
- Pin base image versions (e.g., `node:18-alpine`, not `node:latest`)
- Resource limits must be defined for all containers
- Never expose internal-only ports to the host in production

---

## Security

- Never commit credentials, API keys, or secrets
- Use `.env.local` (gitignored) for sensitive values
- All user input must be validated (Zod schemas in `packages/shared`)
- Follow OWASP guidelines for authentication and authorization
- Report security vulnerabilities privately -- do not open public issues
